metadata.title: Public FDA records with IND information
metadata.scope: Expanding verified reading library, not an exhaustive inventory of public IND material.

crlScreen.method: Case-insensitive IND/investigational-new-drug keyword screen followed by manual passage triage; selected passages verified in original PDFs. Records without those phrases were not manually read in full.

records.summary: Appendix 1 preserves the 2006 pharmacology/toxicology review of the initial IND, subsequent responses, and an amendment. It evaluates safety pharmacology, ADME, repeat-dose toxicology, and the proposed clinical dose escalation.
records.limitation: This is one discipline’s review, not the complete IND. Other appendices cover later development.

records.limitation: These are clinical-development events after initial human dosing. They are not the original nonclinical package or a current dosing guide.

records.summary: The package includes Type B pre-NDA meeting minutes under IND 145628, with questions and FDA responses on nonclinical sufficiency, clinical evidence, and clinical pharmacology. Its history identifies the 2018 first-in-human submission under IND 139023.
records.limitation: This is a late-development meeting, not a first-in-human IND review. The two IND numbers refer to different records within the program.

records.use: See how a sponsor frames questions and how FDA distinguishes preliminary agreement from a final NDA assessment.

records.summary: The retrospective history describes the initial IND hold recommendation, the inadequacy of a literature-only response, and requests for route-specific absorption, interaction, and product-toxicity information. FDA questioned treating DMSO as an inactive excipient.
records.limitation: Historical product-specific requirements, not a current universal study list. The cited text describes a hold recommendation and subsequent deficiencies; it is not a complete original IND.

records.summary: Appendix I includes a February 1999 IND review of rodent carcinogenicity protocols. The reviewer asks for parent-drug and active-metabolite Cmax/AUC measurements and discusses dose selection.
records.limitation: This is later nonclinical development, not the initial human-study package. Nineteen pages are explicitly redacted before this retained review; the IND number is redacted.

sources.evidenceAnchor: Review #2; February 3, 1999; Review and Evaluation of Rodent Carcinogenicity Protocols

records.summary: The initial IND history says animal data supported the starting dose but raised concerns about higher doses because of ocular inflammation. FDA would assess lower-dose human data before escalation. Later discussions address formulation changes and evidence for longer studies.
records.limitation: The history contains inconsistent calendar dates around the initial submission/review; use the sequence of decisions rather than reconstructing exact timing. Initial-IND conclusions are summarized or excerpted within a later BLA review.

records.summary: The history records an initial IND hold for lack of Phase 1 healthy-volunteer data, later lifting, and additional PK/dose-ranging studies after valve changes. CMC discussions addressed delivery, impurities, and device comparability.
records.limitation: A new formulation/device of an established drug. Initial U.S. IND and product bridging do not mean first-ever human exposure to ipratropium.

sources.label: Initial hold and device bridging
sources.evidenceAnchor: Important Milestones in Product Development; IND 45,938

records.summary: The appendix explicitly attaches earlier IND reviews of reproductive/developmental toxicity, in-vivo genotoxicity, and local tolerance. The opening study provides fertility-study design, test material, dose groups, and GLP information.
records.limitation: These retained studies do not establish the full initial IND package or that reproductive studies were needed before every first human dose.

records.summary: The NDA review identifies reproductive and genetic toxicology reviewed with the original 1996 IND submission and lists its pharmacology review as an attachment. Retained text describes the hormone pharmacology and receptor effects.
records.limitation: The appendix is split across the approval package; the linked Part 1 does not contain every later page. The original submission date and the later review date are distinct.

records.summary: The reviewer discusses reuse of an interrupted toxicity study after the compound acquired a therapeutic development path. The discussion refers back to IND-review observations on ocular injury and the limitations of retained study records.
records.limitation: A narrow retrospective IND-linked passage. This source is not itself proof that the complete earlier IND review survives in the online package; QA and incomplete reporting limit interpretation.

records.summary: A December 2008 memorandum preserves sponsor questions and FDA answers on the first vasoconstrictor-assay study. It accepts prior systemic-safety knowledge plus formulation-specific irritation information, then distinguishes bridging and later local-safety work.
records.limitation: An established corticosteroid in a new formulation under a 505(b)(2) strategy, not a new molecular entity. IND identity and some sponsor information are redacted.

sources.evidenceAnchor: SD Type: original submission; Review date: 12-03-08

records.summary: The BLA reviewer explicitly identifies nonclinical safety material excerpted from a 2014 preliminary IND safety review. It shows how prior review work is carried forward, with additional reproductive studies distinguished from the earlier set.
records.limitation: The source excerpt does not establish that every summarized study preceded the first human dose. One earlier table truncates the IND number; the previous-reviews section gives 123788.

sources.label: Attribution to earlier IND safety review
sources.evidenceAnchor: Preliminary safety IND review ... October 10, 2014; excerpted ... included in this BLA review

records.summary: The 1998 original-IND pharmacology review combines animal toxicity, prior human PK/PD, and the proposed patient-study design. Its evaluation links the planned 75 mg maximum to exposure margins and clinical monitoring.
records.limitation: Original U.S. IND does not mean first-in-human: this review already describes previous Phase 1 exposure and proposes a Phase 2 study. Avoid treating its historical margins as general rules.

records.summary: Multiple IND reviews are appended. A 2009 memo recalls initial dosing/exposure restrictions and evaluates whether longer rat/dog studies support an extended rheumatoid-arthritis trial. It weighs reversible, monitorable effects and toxicokinetic margins.
records.limitation: The retained memo concerns an amendment and longer clinical exposure. A reviewer recommendation is not itself the complete regulatory action letter, and later chronic-study expectations are context-specific.

sources.label: Appendix list and 2009 IND memo
sources.evidenceAnchor: Appendix 1; PHARM/TOX MEMO TO FILE; doses up to 10 mg qd

records.summary: The actual 2011 initial-IND review assesses reliance on existing systemic-safety knowledge plus inhalation toxicology. A follow-up memo analyzes impurity specifications and drug stability before and after nebulization during the initial trial.
records.limitation: A new inhalation presentation of an established drug. Some impurity limits are redacted. Historical statements in the memo should not be treated as current impurity guidance.

records.summary: A breakthrough-designation review recounts initial-study authorization and later pre-IND advice for cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma. FDA discusses prior-treatment eligibility, multidisciplinary assessment, separate population analyses, and the meaning of response.
records.limitation: These are disease-expansion and later clinical-development decisions, not a reproduced first-in-human nonclinical review. The document has minor date inconsistencies in later milestone text.

sources.evidenceAnchor: Relevant Regulatory History; September 10, 2015, a pre-IND meeting

records.summary: The FDA assessment explains a partial hold on the Phase 2 component of a combined Phase 1/2 protocol, involving product quality and clinical concerns. Clinical safety, preliminary activity, and expansion-dose rationale supported lifting the hold; diagnostic bridging was also discussed.
records.limitation: A partial hold did not stop every component of the program. Applicant-authored chronology and FDA assessment are labeled separately; the cited FDA assessment supplies the substantive explanation.

sources.label: Chronology and FDA assessment of partial hold
sources.evidenceAnchor: The FDA’s Assessment; insufficient information ... product quality ... 20 mg strength capsule

records.summary: The regulatory history connects the initial single-dose IND with end-of-Phase-1 feedback and a later Phase 2a protocol that FDA considered exploratory. A separate appended statistical review under the IND evaluates long-term carcinogenicity studies.
records.limitation: The absence of an initial hold does not imply agreement with a later efficacy design. Carcinogenicity review belongs to later development; it is not presented as a universal first-dose prerequisite.

records.summary: The integrated package preserves an earlier assessment connecting glass particulate contamination and uncertain injection-site risk to a December 2021 full clinical hold and a nonapproval recommendation. Its history also describes pre-IND advice on alternative injectable formulations.
records.limitation: The product was subsequently approved; the cited hold/nonapproval passage is an earlier review embedded in the package. It does not establish that particles caused every injection-site reaction. NDA 215974 covers the oral presentation.

records.summary: An appended IND review retains end-of-Phase-2 questions and answers. It distinguishes dermal toxicology supporting a 12-week trial from longer studies supporting an extension and eventual NDA, including the timing of ongoing animal exposure.
records.limitation: Later IND development of a new topical route, not the original first-dose review. Agreement on study design remained conditional on review of final reports.

records.summary: The regulatory history records a January 2021 initial full hold because FDA lacked a protocol, sufficient CMC information, investigator information, and an investigator’s brochure. It dates the complete response and hold removal, then separates subsequent EUA/NDA planning.
records.limitation: This is a retrospective account, not the complete hold letter or original IND. These administrative/scientific omissions should not be misrepresented as evidence that the molecule itself failed toxicology.

sources.evidenceAnchor: January 25, 2021 ... full clinical hold ... February 23, 2021

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Unapproved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 01/09/2026
records.summary: The January 2026 letter explains why heterogeneity, treatment confounding, and study design limited interpretation of the single-arm ALLELE study. FDA offers to review a detailed new protocol under the existing IND, including the choice of control.
records.limitation: This is a BLA nonapproval letter and a proposed route back to IND-stage study planning. It is not an IND refusal or an original IND review. Snapshot status is application-specific, not a global statement about the therapy.

sources.label: Why another study may be needed
sources.evidenceAnchor: a randomized controlled study may be necessary; detailed draft protocol under the existing ... IND

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Unapproved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 02/07/2026
records.summary: The 2026 letter explicitly traces concerns across pre-IND, IND, and BLA meetings: identifying neuronopathic MPS II, comparing the external-control population, and interpreting a novel CSF biomarker threshold. Agreement in principle on a protocol did not resolve those evidence questions.
records.limitation: A marketing-application assessment, not the full earlier meeting record. Some meeting details are redacted. Unapproved is the FDA dataset’s snapshot classification for this application.

sources.label: Prior development advice and remaining uncertainty
sources.evidenceAnchor: expressed concerns ... at the Pre-IND, IND, and BLA meetings

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Unapproved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 04/10/2026
records.summary: The 2026 letter quotes 2021 IND-meeting advice to isolate each component’s contribution in a combination and later advice on interpretability of response. It connects those earlier concerns to the BLA assessment of a heterogeneous single-arm population.
records.limitation: This is a later FDA account quoting earlier advice; the entire IND meeting package is not reproduced. The requested combination’s nonapproval is not an IND hold.

sources.label: IND-meeting advice on contribution and design
sources.evidenceAnchor: Type B meeting dated March 25, 2021; contribution of each component

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Unapproved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 01/23/2024
records.summary: FDA says a publication alone did not provide analyzable efficacy and safety data for independent review. The letter explains that referencing another holder’s IND information requires a Letter of Authorization.
records.limitation: A nonapproval of this specific application, not a statement that all phenobarbital products are unapproved. This is an NDA-stage evidence-access lesson rather than an earlier IND-review extract.

sources.label: Analyzable data and IND authorization
sources.evidenceAnchor: Letter of Authorization from the holder of that IND

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 06/17/2021
records.summary: The 2021 CRL recounts 2016–2019 IND-development advice about the definition, reliability, and validity of the NPC severity scale. It explains how unresolved measurement concerns affected the later assessment of treatment benefit.
records.limitation: The application is listed Approved in the later dataset; this letter records an earlier nonapproval. It does not establish the current approved indication or provide the full eventual approval rationale.

sources.label: IND-phase endpoint advice
sources.evidenceAnchor: 5DNPCCSS Regulatory History; Despite our advice during the IND phase

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 03/22/2019
records.summary: An additional product-quality comment recalls advice beginning at a 2006 pre-IND meeting about pH and impurity limits under the USP monograph. It shows that a CMC issue can persist across multiple development interactions.
records.limitation: The source explicitly calls this particular monograph comment a non-approvability issue; do not present it as the reason for the CRL. Other deficiencies are listed separately. Historical application snapshot: Approved.

sources.label: Pre-IND-to-NDA compendial discussion
sources.evidenceAnchor: comment/recommendation that is not an approvability issue; Pre-IND meeting dated September 20, 2006

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 02/09/2024
records.summary: FDA distinguishes compatibility data generated for an IND formulation, XP-9164, from the Gvoke vial formulation proposed in the supplement. It requests evidence on the actual product and administration conditions, including comparative physical behavior.
records.limitation: The CRL addresses a supplement for IV diagnostic use. The original product’s approval and the FDA dataset’s Approved label do not mean that this proposed use was approved by this letter.

sources.label: Formulation-specific compatibility and stability
sources.evidenceAnchor: Compatibility studies under IND 156281 used XP-9164, not the proposed Gvoke vial formulation

sources.label: Scientific bridge for the proposed use
sources.evidenceAnchor: Clinical pharmacology and scientific-bridge questions

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 05/06/2016
records.summary: The 2016 letter refers to an IND advice request rejecting an alternative efficacy analysis if the positive control failed. It asks for a repeat inguinal-region study with adequate controls after one pivotal study failed its prespecified endpoint.
records.limitation: A later CRL referencing earlier IND advice; it is not the original advice letter. The product appears in the Approved snapshot after subsequent development.

sources.label: Prespecified analysis and prior IND advice
sources.evidenceAnchor: IND 076549, Advice/Information Request, April 17, 2015

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 12/17/2021
records.summary: The 2021 letter lists repeated IND meetings emphasizing durable efficacy in eosinophilic esophagitis. It explains why short-term histologic and symptom findings did not answer the long-term question then under review.
records.limitation: The application later appears Approved. Read this as a historical assessment of the requested evidence and regimen; it does not summarize the later approved label.

sources.label: Durability questions raised during IND development
sources.evidenceAnchor: communications under IND 103173; benefit of long-term treatment

records.approvalStatus: openFDA snapshot: Approved (dataset updated 2026-08-13); cited letter 01/20/2023
records.summary: The letter distinguishes cord-blood units meeting licensure criteria from units from ineligible donors that may be used under an IND for urgent medical need. FDA requests revised procedures and forms preserving that distinction.
records.limitation: A BLA-stage quality/licensure issue with a specific investigational-use pathway, not an initial efficacy-trial review. The pathway should not be generalized to all biological products.

sources.label: Licensure versus urgent investigational use
sources.evidenceAnchor: such units may be made available ... under an investigational new drug application
